title: John Hurt
wiki_lead:
Sir John Vincent Hurt (22 January 1940 – 25 January 2017) was an English actor. Regarded as one of the finest actors of his generation and described as having the "most distinctive voice in Britain", he was referred to by David Lynch as "simply the greatest actor in the world". Hurt's career spanned more than five decades. During that time, he was the recipient of numerous accolades, including four BAFTAs and a Golden Globe, in addition to nominations for two Academy Awards. He was knighted in 2015 for services to drama.
Hurt graduated from the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in 1962. He appeared in a handful of films before obtaining his breakthrough role, as Richard Rich in the Academy Award winning film A Man for All Seasons (1966), a few years later. It was in the mid-1970s that his career really took off. After a highly acclaimed performance alongside Richard Attenborough and Judy Geeson in 10 Rillington Place (1971), receiving a nomination for the British Academy Television Award for Best Supporting Actor, he then won the British Academy Television Award for Best Actor for The Naked Civil Servant (1975), and played Caligula in the BBC TV series I, Claudius (1976). Hurt earned Academy Award nominations for Best Supporting Actor for Midnight Express (1978), and for Best Actor for The Elephant Man (1980). Other films he had large roles in include Alien (1979), Heaven's Gate (1980), Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984), White Mischief (1987), Scandal (1989), The Field (1990), King Ralph (1991), Rob Roy (1995), and Contact (1997).
Hurt gained further prominence portraying Garrick Ollivander in the Harry Potter film series (2001–11), as well as appearing in the 2004 and 2008 Hellboy films, V for Vendetta (2005), Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull (2008), Outlander (2008), and Snowpiercer (2013). He also acted in the acclaimed films Melancholia (2011), Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (2011), Only Lovers Left Alive (2013) and Jackie (2016). He reprised his role as Quentin Crisp in An Englishman in New York (2009), which brought his seventh BAFTA nomination. He portrayed an incarnation of the Doctor known as the War Doctor in Doctor Who, a role he later reprised in audio dramas for Big Finish Productions. He voiced roles in Watership Down (1978), The Lord of the Rings (1978), The Plague Dogs (1982), The Black Cauldron (1985), Dogville (2003), Valiant (2005), Merlin (2008–2012), The Gruffalo's Child (2011), and Thomas & Friends: Sodor's Legend of the Lost Treasure (2015), and narrated the BBC documentary series Human Planet and Planet Dinosaur.

Life and career


Early years and education
John Vincent Hurt was born on 22 January 1940, in Chesterfield, Derbyshire, the son of Arnould Herbert Hurt (1904–1999) and Phyllis (née Massey; 1907–1975). grok_lead: Sir John Vincent Hurt CBE (22 January 1940 â 25 January 2017) was an English stage and screen actor distinguished by his gravelly voice and ability to portray introspective, often anguished characters across genres from drama to science fiction. Hurt debuted in film with The Wild and the Willing in 1962 and built a prolific career encompassing over 200 productions, including television and voice work, marked by a preference for roles that delved into human vulnerability and moral ambiguity. His breakthrough performances included Max in Midnight Express (1978), earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor, and the disfigured Joseph Merrick in The Elephant Man (1980), which brought a Best Actor nomination and critical praise for its empathetic physicality. Hurt's genre-defining turns extended to Kane in Alien (1979), whose visceral chestburster scene became a horror milestone, and Winston Smith in Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984), capturing dystopian despair. Later highlights featured Garrick Ollivander in the Harry Potter series and voice roles such as Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings (1978 animated adaptation), alongside honors including the 2012 BAFTA for Outstanding British Contribution to Cinema.
